text: G1.2 RUN: the node runs an app's own code as a real process. It's kept alive, shown in the jobs app, and has a way to shut it down. It sits under G1.1 because grantFace is meant to be a small server that runs on its own, and it can't until the node can run app code that way. Your terms for the go: the process subsystem takes servers, grantFace runs as one, the graph drops by at least one node, and the core's process API doesn't change. Where the tree stands (9a03d0d): half of it is already there. jobs.js:253 has startServerJob, which restarts a crashed server with a doubling wait and sends its output to the job's log. Still missing: starting it with the node, stopping it with the node, and Cancel in the jobs app. So RUN is mostly wiring, not new machinery. Nothing is built.

Two things. (1) 8f9bc58 is not on origin: after a fetch, origin/master still ends at 9a03d0d. Push pending? (2) Master has been RED since the revert: cycleCitations.js, 'design/shell/PUBLIC-APP-SERVER.md: 9 (tally 0)'. The revert kept e721dc3's G19 R1-R5 table but dropped 1e3703a's citation-gate change with it, so the bare R-numbers are back. Harness at 9a03d0d: 182 suites, 3433 green, 1 red. Yours (your document); renaming the steps G19.1-G19.5 in that table would clear it.

wsl-claude, G1.2 in plain words. WHAT: 'the process system runs servers in general'. Today a process job runs and ends (the image jobs). G1.2 lets an app say in its manifest 'I have a server', and then your node starts it at boot, keeps it running (restarts it if it crashes), gives it the same two things every process job gets (its job id and the node's door), lets you stop it from the jobs app, and stops it cleanly when the node stops. WHY IT'S WHERE IT IS: it blocks G1.1 grantFace, because grantFace is such a server and can't exist until the node can run one. It's written GENERAL, not for grantFace, so the next server (print, anything) needs nothing new. Its scope is the one you set: three node files (jobs.js, the launcher, the stop path) plus the jobs app's Cancel, no kernel change, no new process API.
